# Release verification test vectors

Produced by **the real minisign 0.11**, not by this repository's code, so
`test_verify_release.py` checks interoperability rather than self-consistency.
Regenerating them with our own implementation would make the tests prove only
that we agree with ourselves.

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| `omp-gateway-0.1.0.tar.gz` | stand-in artifact (plain text - the format is irrelevant to a signature) |
| `omp-gateway-0.1.0.tar.gz.minisig` | valid signature, prehashed (`ED`) - minisign's default |
| `omp-gateway-0.1.0.tar.gz.legacy.minisig` | valid signature, legacy (`Ed`, `minisign -l`) |
| `rewritten-comment.minisig` | the valid signature with its **trusted comment edited** - the file signature still verifies, the global signature does not. `minisign -V` rejects it with "Comment signature verification failed"; so must we |
| `release.pub` | the key that signed them |
| `attacker.pub` | an unrelated key, for the wrong-key path |
| `SHA256SUMS`, `SHA256SUMS.minisig` | a signed checksum file |

**The secret keys were deleted and never committed.** These vectors are
public by construction: a public key and signatures over a file that ships
beside them. Nothing here signs anything real, and no OMP release key exists
yet - when one does, it is generated by the maintainer and never appears in
this repository.

Regenerate with:

```bash
minisign -G -p release.pub -s sk.key -W
minisign -S -s sk.key -m omp-gateway-0.1.0.tar.gz -t "OMP 0.1.0 …" -W
minisign -S -l -s sk.key -m omp-gateway-0.1.0.tar.gz \
  -x omp-gateway-0.1.0.tar.gz.legacy.minisig -t "OMP 0.1.0 legacy format" -W
rm sk.key      # do not commit it
```
